> 同人。同人于野，亨。利涉大川，利君子貞。

The thirteenth hexagram is about shared ground, and the text measures it four times at four widths.

## 同 is a gathering

說文: 同，合會也。從𠔼從口.

The original sense is converging, assembling.

The familiar explanation — "one shared mouth, one shared speech" — is a reading of the 口 component. It works as an interpretation, but the dictionary's own gloss is simply 合會.

And here a caution the book keeps repeating: 同 and 合 are not distinguished in the dictionary. 合, 說文 合口也, is to close the mouth, thence to join. Both originals sit on the side of gathering.

The distinction this book makes is a distinction of use, not of etymology: 同 points to shared direction (minds in accord), 合 points to being joined together (assembled by external force). A reader should know which kind of claim is being made.

## Four widths

野: 說文 野，郊外也 — beyond the suburb. Under the Zhou arrangement: 國 (the capital), 郊, 野. 野 is the open ground past the suburb, with no clan, no bloodline, no faction boundary.

And the hexagram measures the same act at four widths:

- 門 — the gate (line 1)
- 宗 — the lineage (line 2)
- 郊 — the near outskirts (line 6)
- 野 — the open ground (the judgement)

From inner to outer, each wider than the last. The judgements run the other way: 于門 無咎, 于宗 吝, 于郊 無悔, 于野 亨.

Which is the entire argument in one line of text: sharing within the gate is not wrong, sharing within the lineage is already small, and sharing in the open is the only one that can carry you across a river.

## 伏戎于莽

莽: 說文 莽，南昌謂犬善逐兔艸中為莽 — the grass where a dog runs down a rabbit. Dense cover.

九三 伏戎于莽，升其高陵，三歲不興 — weapons hidden in the grass, climbed to the high mound, and three years without rising.

Three years is not a duration. It is the shape of a posture: hiding and watching is stable, and stable postures do not end on their own.

## 乘其墉，弗克攻

墉: 說文 墉，城垣也.

九四 has climbed the wall and does not attack. 吉.

The line is a rare thing in the book: the correct outcome is the non-event. Having the position and the force, and not using them.

## 先號咷而後笑

號 is the cry of pain; 咷 is weeping that will not stop.

九五 同人，先號咷而後笑，大師克相遇.

First the weeping, then the laugh, and an army in between.

This is the hexagram's most honest line. The meeting of minds does not happen without the earlier grief of not meeting, and it does not happen without force — 大師 — clearing what stood in the way.

So the emotional sequence is not decoration. It is the mechanism: the cry is what the blockage costs, and the laugh comes after something has been overcome.

## 類族辨物

The 象's instruction: 君子以類族辨物 — classify the kinds, distinguish the things.

Note what it is not. It is not "treat all things as one." The shared ground is made by drawing distinctions correctly, not by erasing them.

Which is why 同人 and 合 are different projects. 合 assembles by removing the difference. 同 works because the difference has been placed accurately, and then the ground can be shared.

## The test

Take a group you consider "your people." Ask at which width it exists: the gate, the lineage, the near outskirts, or the open ground. Then ask the harder question — whether the width it actually has would let an outsider in, or only let the existing members stay comfortable.
